back_translation: The burden-oracle concerning the Valley of Vision: What has happened to you, that all of you have gone up onto the rooftops?
O city full of uproar, city of revelry, exultant town! Your slain were not slain by the sword, nor did they die in battle.
All your rulers fled together; they were captured without a bow being used. All of yours who were found were captured together, though they had fled far away.
Therefore I said: "Turn your eyes away from me; let me weep bitterly. Do not press me with consolation over the ruin of the daughter of my people."
For the Lord GOD of Hosts has appointed a day — a day of tumult and trampling and confusion in the Valley of Vision, a day of battering down walls and of crying out to the mountain.
Elam carries the quiver, coming with chariots and horsemen, and Kir uncovers the shield.
Your choicest valleys are full of chariots, and the horsemen take up positions at the city gate.
He has stripped away the covering of Judah; and in that day you looked to the weapons of the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
You saw the many breaches in the wall of the City of David, and you stored up the water of the lower pool.
You counted the houses of Jerusalem and tore houses down to reinforce the wall.
You built a holding reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool — but you did not look to Him who made this, and you did not see Him who fashioned it long ago.
In that day the Lord GOD of Hosts called for weeping and lamentation, for shaved heads and the girding of sackcloth.
But behold — there is mirth and gladness instead: killing of cattle and slaughtering of sheep, eating of meat and drinking of wine, saying, "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!"
The LORD of Hosts has revealed it in my ears: "This iniquity will not be atoned for you until you die," — thus the Sovereign Master, the LORD of Hosts, has spoken.
The Sovereign Master, the LORD of Hosts, says this: "Go to this steward, to Shebna the palace administrator, and say:
What right do you have here, and whom do you have here, that you have hewn out a tomb for yourself here — carving your resting place on the height, chiseling a dwelling for yourself in the rock?
Behold, O strong man! The LORD is about to hurl you away violently; He will grip you firmly,
roll you up tightly into a round ball, and throw you like a ball into a wide-open land. There you will die, and there your splendid chariots will remain — O you disgrace of your master's court!
I will push you out of your office, and you will be pulled down from your station.
And in that day I will call My servant, Eliakim son of Hilkiah.

I will clothe him with your robe and fasten your sash firmly on him, and I will place your governing authority in his hand. He will be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
I will place the key of the house of David on his shoulder: what he opens, no one can shut; and what he shuts, no one can open.
I will drive him in like a peg in a firm place, and he will become a throne of honor for the house of his father.
They will hang on him all the honor of his father's house — the descendants and the offshoots, all the small vessels, from the basins to every single jar.
The LORD of Hosts declares: In that day the peg driven into the firm place will work loose; it will be cut down and fall, and the load hanging on it will be cut off. For the LORD has spoken.
